evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: 字形演變; 甲骨文合集8159; 金文集成04140; 說文小篆
evidence.text: The database records 休 in an oracle-bone example (合集8159), a bronze inscription example (集成04140), and the Shuowen seal-script category. Its account identifies the left element as a person seen from the side and 木 as a tree, interpreting the whole graph as a person resting against a tree. The page does not date the individual cited artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢字「休」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle-bone and bronze forms; cited textual examples
evidence.text: The account reads the early graph as 人 plus 木 and interprets it as resting in a tree's shade. It says the person faces away from the trunk; some 木 tops lean toward the person to suggest shade. Although that shape can resemble 禾, the source identifies it as 木. It traces shade and shelter senses, blessing/goodness, and stopping/resting as related uses, citing bronze inscriptions and received texts. These are the source's analyses, not independently verified semantic chronology; no inscription image was visually inspected in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 as transcribed by 漢典
evidence.text: Shuowen defines 休 as “息止也” and explains its graph as 从人依木 (“from a person relying on wood/tree”); it records 庥 as an alternate form with 广. This is an early lexicographic interpretation, not direct proof of the graph's original semantic motivation.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 as transcribed by 漢典
evidence.field: 康熙字典; citations of 尚書, 詩經, 禮記
evidence.text: The later Kangxi entry quotes 休 in the sense ‘good/blessing’ from 尚書·太甲 and 詩·商頌, glosses it also as pardon, and cites rest/stopping in 禮·月令. It also lists leave-taking and retirement. These examples establish multiple traditional senses but do not by themselves order their historical development. The Shuowen annotation additionally quotes 詩·周南: “南有喬木，不可休思.”
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 字形; 金文 interpretation; competing analysis
evidence.text: 字通 disputes the Shuowen/tree-rest analysis. It proposes that the 木-like element was originally 禾-shaped and represented paired marker posts at a military gate, with 休 denoting recognition of military merit before them; it cites a bronze inscription use glossed ‘good/commendation.’ It rejects Shuowen's shape and meaning account. The page also reports, as a different proposal, Guo Moruo's rest-in-the-fields interpretation and objects that soldiers would not deliberately choose cultivated fields to rest in. These are competing scholarly interpretations; the page alone does not settle them.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; semantic extensions and attestations
evidence.text: The source proposes a semantic chain from shade to shelter/protection, then to benefaction or bestowed reward, and associates pleasure and goodness with resting under shade; it separately connects resting under a tree with stopping. It cites bronze inscriptions for protection, reward, goodness, and stopping, including 剌鼎, 效卣, 員鼎, and 噩侯鼎, and received texts such as 詩經 and 漢書. This is a source-proposed linkage, not a fully dated chronology. It calls 茠 a differentiated graph for the shade sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.field: rows 3878–3879; Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese and Middle Chinese for 休
evidence.text: The exact local rows give 休 xiū, Middle Chinese xjuw, Old Chinese *qʰ(r)u, with glosses ‘rest (v.)’ and ‘blessing.’ These are Baxter–Sagart dataset values. The local source is not itself an external citation; the corresponding external reading for the character was checked against the listed Unihan record URL, which was inaccessible to the web tool during this research.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.text: The source analyzes 休 as 人 plus 木, both semantic in its account; neither is proposed as a phonetic component. Therefore this entry does not require an ancient sound match between 木 or 人 and 休. The local Baxter–Sagart reading for 休 is *qʰ(r)u (MC xjuw), while 木 is *C.mˤok and 人 is *ni[ŋ], in the same dataset; this is consistent with treating neither as the sound component, without independently proving graphic roles.

gaps: The cited paleographic catalogs identify oracle-bone and bronze examples, including 合集8159 and bronze examples, but no inscription image was visually inspected; individual artifact dates and readings were not independently verified here.

The first attested semantic use cannot be ranked confidently from dictionary gloss lists. Although oracle-bone graph attestations are cataloged and bronze uses include ‘good/blessing,’ accessible sources do not establish a securely dated sequence from shade/rest to protection, benefaction, and goodness.

There is a material disagreement: CUHK and Sinica support person-under-tree/resting, while 字通 proposes 禾-like military marker posts and ceremonial commendation, rejecting Shuowen's account. The retrieved pages do not provide enough primary inscription context to resolve it.

The precise ancient shape of the 木-like element remains debated in the accessed secondary analyses: CUHK explicitly says it is 木 despite occasional resemblance to 禾, while 字通 argues for an original 禾-shaped component. No glyph image inspection was conducted.

Official Unicode Unihan character-specific URLs were attempted but returned internal errors. Local kMandarin readings were cross-checked, but the contract's requested official-record click-through could not be validated by web retrieval.

No sound component is proposed by the reviewed analyses, so there is no independent object-name or phonetic-loan claim to assess. The local Baxter–Sagart dataset supports 休 *qʰ(r)u / MC xjuw and nonmatching component readings for 木 and 人; those values do not establish the graph interpretation.
